utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to wish everybody in this courtroom [Technical difficulty] ask the Registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. For the transcript, I would like the presentation of the parties, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, David Akerson and on my right is Jason Dominguez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Appearances for the Defence side, please. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Good afternoon, Your Honour, Tjarda van der Spoel, Defence counsel, accompanied by my legal assistant Mr. Julius von Bone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. van der Spoel. You may sit down. This is the first hearing we are holding in this case, and I would like the Prosecution to make its opening statement and present its case. Mr. Akerson, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I -- there is just one administrative housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Defence counsel has graciously stipulated to the authenticity and the admissibility of the exhibits which are audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation] Does the French booth not -- is the French booth having trouble? Can you hear what is being said?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, the French booth cannot hear what's going on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [In English] there is a minor technical problem.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Two booths were working at the same time. It should be all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Akerson, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There has been a stipulation as to the exhibits, the authenticity and the admissibility of the exhibits, the audio files. These are recorded -- a recorded telephone call and intercepted telephone calls, and I would like to just read into the record those exhibits, the one that is have been stipulated to, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before proceeding, I would like to remind you that according to the minutes of the hearing pursuant to Rule 65 ter, the Defence only raised an issue relating to interpretation and the Defence counsel clearly indicated that this -- there is a minor difference leer and that it is only a minor difference. Isn't that right, Mr. Akerson? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Yes, Mr. President. There was a difference between the translations of the interceptions and that was an issue -- a point I made during the pre-trial meeting; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Yes. And you said that it's a minor discrepancy. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Yes. And we have received new translations from the Prosecutor's office and we do not disagree on those translations. So that's the only point of difference we had concerning the translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: But you are contesting the legality of these intercepts? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: No, we are not, we are not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Mr. Akerson, are you saying that the Defence has objected to the authenticity of these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not, Your Honour. I am saying that they have stipulated. I would actually like to tender these into evidence now so that is done and we don't have to deal with that during the trial, just to make it more efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So the decision pertaining to the admissibility or not is a decision that will be rendered at a latter stage. We are not going to be rendering that decision right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Okay. May I presume that they are tendered into evidence, though, so I can use them as if they were already tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And I would like the Registrar to give us the numbers here please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first would be P1 MFI. That will be trial Exhibit No. 01, the audio. That will be P1 MFI. The 1A will be the audio; 1E will be the English translation; and 1A will be the Albanian translation. P2 MFI will be the audio; 2E will be the English translation; and 2A will be the Albanian translation. P3 MFI would be the audio; 2E will be the English; and 3A will be the Albanian translation. P4 MFI would be the audio, P4E would be the English. The third would be P3 MFI; the fourth would be P4 MFI; and the fifth will be P5 MFI. Number 6 would be P6 MFI. Number 7 would be P7 MFI. Number 8 would be P8 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Yes, number 9? Okay? [Interpretation] Mr. Akerson, I think we are done now, as far as these exhibits are concerned. Do you have any other procedural matters you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Only, Your Honours, that we are intending on displaying a few computer slides during the opening and I would ask that you be prepared to select the computer evidence button that's on your computer, and to the booth that we are going to be using --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Have you given the translation booths this material, i.e. the intercepts?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I do believe so, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. May I ask you to start with your opening statement now.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: May it please the Court and Defence counsel. Over the course of the next few days, the OTP will present to you evidence that proves that Beqa Beqaj, the accused, interfered with a witness and a potential witness in the Limaj trial. In so doing he committed contempt of court under Rule 77. This case is primarily a case of witness interference and bribery as opposed to threats or intimidations. There were two targets of this interference. They are known in this case by their pseudonyms, B1 and his close relative B2. B1 is the principal victim. The essential facts of this case are simple. Between June and November of 2004, Beqa Beqaj repeatedly sought - six times that we know of - to convince B1 and B2 to withdraw their testimony against the Limaj accused. You will hear evidence that B1 is a critical witness in the Limaj case. In July of 1998, B1 was abducted and taken to a makeshift prison camp in the village of Lapusnik in Kosovo. Prisoners in this camp were brutalised, tortured and murdered. As the camp disbanded, approximately 21 prisoners were marched into the mountains. The guards divided the 21 prisoners into two groups, one that was released and the other that was to be massacred. 12 unlucky prisoners were in the second group, including B1. They were lined up, a death sentence was pronounced, the guards opened fire on the defenceless prisoners. B1 survives this massacre by fleeing into the woods in a hail of bullets. You will hear that B1 is a critical witness. He's a critical witness because he can testify to the acts of all three Limaj accused at Lapusnik. He can testify firsthand to the beatings and torture that were given to him by two of the three Limaj accused. And he can testify as an eyewitness to the massacre. B1 was and is a critical witness in the Limaj case. B1's importance in the Limaj case is the motive for the interference in this case. Beqa Beqaj is the means by which the interferences are perpetrated. You will hear evidence that Beqaj at all times relevant to this indictment attempted to directly communicate with B1 without assistance. B1 has been in witness protection since 2003 because of previous threats to B1's safety. He's had two assassination attempts, repeated direct threats of violence and even death if he testified, and threats given to his friends and family. His protection measures that were awarded him or given to him included moving him to a new secret location in the country to which he had already fled; providing him with new telephone numbers; and giving him 24-hour close protection, or 24-hour armed guards. At this stage, only his closest family members knew where he was and were able to contact him. This is where Beqa Beqaj enters our story. Beqa Beqaj was orphaned as a young boy and B1's father took in Beqaj and Beqaj spent much time with B1's family. Beqaj knew B1's family and the family knew Beqaj. Beqaj had the means to reach B1 by using list family contacts. And Beqaj had another ominous connection: He was related by marriage to Isak Musliu, one of the Limaj accused. Now, turning our attention to June of 2004, the times relevant to our indictment. The start of the Limaj trial is about six months away and Beqaj commits the first of his six interferences. On June 6th, Bashkim Beqaj, who is Beqa Beqaj's son, accosts Witness B2. B2 again is a relative of B1. Bashkim is aggressive and he blames B2 for Isak Musliu being on trial and for being in The Hague. B2 is 68 and Bashkim Beqaj is in his early 20s. Luckily, bystanders are there to intervene and prevent any escalation of that violence. B2 goes directly from this encounter and demands an explanation from Beqaj and Beqaj gives him one. And the explanation is: that Isak Musliu has contacted Beqaj six times and demanded that he go to B2 and demanded that he -- that Beqaj withdraw his statement -- that Beqaj get B2 to withdraw his statement, sorry. B2 is also offered land if he withdraws his statement. Early September, two months before the Limaj trial, the second interference takes place. Now B1 of course is in witness protection and unreachable. So Beqaj has to use his family connections to make contact. Beqaj uses a relative of B1's to convey the following message: that Beqaj is acting on behalf of Musliu, that Musliu would give him land if he withdrew his statement. September 27th, interference number 3. Beqa Beqaj visits B1's relative and asks that relative to relay a message: that Beqaj was speaking on behalf of Fatmir Limaj and Isak Musliu, that they wanted B1 to travel back to Kosovo urgently to meet with the Limaj lawyers, and that he should withdraw his statement. The relative wanted to give B1 the number of Beqaj so they could speak directly. B1 refused to take the number and refused to withdraw his testimony. Later that day, interference number 4. Beqaj, dissatisfied with B1's refusal to cooperate with his earlier request, communicates a second time that B1 must go at great speed to Kosovo to meet with the lawyers, the family of the accused, as well as Beqaj and withdraw his statement. During this period, of course, B1 is in regular communication with the ICTY investigators who are preparing the case. B1 tells the investigators about these communications that he's getting so our investigators set up a recorded call to capture what is happening with B1. And that brings us to interference number 5: a call recorded by between 1 and Beqa Beqaj. Takes place on October 6th. It's about a month and a half before the start of the Limaj trial. And you will hear the audio recording of this conversation. Similar to the previous interferences, the essence of the call is that Beqa doesn't want B1 to testify. But in this case you will hear the actual language used by Beqaj. He says, Come meet with Limaj's brother and say you had nothing to do with Limaj or Musliu. He says, Fix something up. Give us some help. As a result of this call, the OTP decides to conduct further investigation. We seek and we obtain a wire-tap of Beqaj's phone. You will hear several of these recorded intercepted phone calls. In these calls, Beqa uses -- Beqaj uses coded language to discuss witnesses. These conversations are the plans and they are the logistics of getting to these witnesses. And Beqaj is involved. In the most significant of these calls, you will hear interference number 6, a recorded call between Beqaj and B1 on October 13th. In this call, Beqaj is again trying to interfere with B1's truthful testimony. Beqaj again asks B1 to come back to Kosovo urgently to Kosovo to meet with lawyers and/or Demir Limaj, Fatmir Limaj's brother, to make a statement that repudiates his earlier statement. In this call they're clearly discussing B1's evidence that he is to give at this institution, that he can give against Limaj and Musliu. Most importantly in this recording, Beqaj says the following: "We are not pressuring you as to Bala," Bala being one of the three Limaj accused. "We are not pressuring you as to Bala." You will hear evidence from ICTY investigator Jonathan Sutch who interviews Beqa Beqaj twice after these intercepted calls are reviewed and analysed by the OTP. He's interviewed twice, on October 19th and the 21st. In the first interview, Sutch begins the interview by advising Beqaj of his rights including his right to counsel. And at that point, Beqaj makes a spontaneous admission. He says, I don't need a lawyer because I've only spoken to one witness. He admits he's spoken to one of our witnesses. Sutch continues with the advisal and conducts the interview in which Beqa then denies all knowledge of witnesses in our trials, all knowledge of B1 and B2 in particular, denies having any contact with any witness or potential witnesses. You will hear evidence two days later that Sutch conducts the second interview and this time Beqaj is represented by counsel. And in this interview Beqaj's story changes. In the interview Beqaj initially, again, denies any involvement with witnesses. But ultimately, after questioning, admits that, yes, he did have a conversation with B1 and, yes, he did have a conversation with Musliu about B1. And you will hear those sections of that interview. That is the evidence in this case, Your Honours. It won't take us long to present it. But it will clearly show that Beqa Beqaj interfered with a witness in the Limaj trial and a potential witness in the Limaj trial and it will show that he did so knowingly and it will show that he did so wilfully. Under Rule 77, you have the inherent power to protect your proceedings, to protect what are your witnesses, to protect your trials, and we are going to ask that at the end of this case, that you do just that by finding Beqa Beqaj guilty. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Akerson. I believe that the Defence counsel is about to make its opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Mr. President, Your Honours, Prosecutor. In the pre-trial Defence brief, the Defence has already pointed out the distinction should be made between the accused Beqaj and the other accused in former content cases. The Defence submits that when prosecuting an ignorant individual, as my client, the Prosecutor's standard and burden of proof must be scrutinised carefully, in any event more carefully than in the event an officer of the court would be prosecuted. In this case, it is up to the Prosecutor to establish that the accused is aware of the existence of Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and that the acts or omissions of the accused are contrary to that rule. In addition, the Prosecutor must prove that Beqa Beqaj knowingly and wilfully interfered with the Tribunal's administration of justice. Also, the Prosecution must prove that Beqa Beqaj had knowledge of the facts that the person in question or persons in questions, are potential witnesses who are giving evidence in the case the Prosecutor is claiming, or is about to give evidence in those proceedings. Furthermore, Your Honours, the Prosecutor must establish that the accused, by his act or omission, participated in the crime envisaged and that this amounts to an attempt or incitement as contained in the indictment. Lastly, all these elements must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The Defence holds that the Prosecution has until now, and will not in the future, bring forward a case in which above-mentioned elements are proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. van der Spoel. If I have understood you correctly, Mr. Beqaj would like to make a statement at this point in time, or perhaps at a latter stage. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: At this point in time would be very fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So I give the floor to Mr. Beqaj so that he can make his opening statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Honoured Judges, my imprisonment is unjust. First of all, I didn't offer any land or money to anyone. This is all a lie. Secondly, I didn't call anyone on the phone. They stated themselves. As for justice to be served, he has to be here and imprisoned here and not me. My imprisonment -- from the time I have been imprisoned, I had no contacts with Albanians. You have prohibited me from using my own language. I am imprisoned in the same room with Serbs. I don't see any justice here in this trial. As of 1971, I have supported my six-member family. From this year until 2000, I have worked abroad and in 2003, on 15th of November, I returned from Slovenia. I didn't go to anyone's house and to anyone's door to accuse someone or to make someone call me. This is by their own wish, and their promises and their statements are all registered. He said -- he stated that he has nothing against Fatmir Limaj and Isak Musliu. Neither Isak Musliu nor Fatmir Limaj offered me money or land and they didn't tell me to go to his relative or to call him and persuade him to testify -- not to testify against him. This is all unjust basis for me being in prison. All I ask is here to release me and allow me to support my family. I never was anyone's thug, and I never worked for money. I always worked throughout my life. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Beqaj. Rest assured this Tribunal is endeavouring to do everything it can to render justice in the shortest possible time. However, I have a remark to make to Mr. van der Spoel and this concerns what Mr. Beqaj said. He complained about his detention and stated that he was together in the same room with other people, other people with whom he doesn't get on so well. Therefore, if you wish to make any particular comment regarding his detention, I advise you to file a motion and send it to the department responsible for the detention of the accused, and this in the shortest possible time. And I'm convinced that they will respond in the most appropriate manner. That said, I believe that we should now hear the first witness, and we must drop the blinds so that the witness can walk into the courtroom. I believe that the usher will be bringing the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you hear what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before testifying, it is necessary for you to take the solemn declaration, according to the Rules. The usher will show you the text of the solemn declaration. Usher, could you read out the text and the witness could repeat it. Please, could you put the microphone on. Is everything all right? Please go ahead, then. Usher, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I abide to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but could you please repeat what the usher said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution would now like to put some questions to you. Mr. Akerson, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: Jason Dominguez for OTP. I would like to confirm that we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: For the identification, we will go to closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dominguez, you may proceed. In the meantime, Mr. Dominguez, I advise you to tell the witness that if he feels he is going to either disclose his identity or the identity of another witness, please ask him that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you -- Witness, if you need to make an answer to a question that reveals your name and identity or the name and identity of the other witness in this case, please let the Court know and we can go back into private session. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Yes. Everything is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had a sheet that had the pseudonyms for this case that we had on the witness stand. Can we find that and replace that there for him, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: You want to tender the sheet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, B1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: This is just for the witness to take a look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember the instruction on using the pseudonyms B1 and B2 in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. How do you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know Beqa Beqaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: When I reached the working age, I have known Beqa ever since. We've spent time together, and there was nothing bad between us, ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he has any children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He has children, but I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of his children, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Only Bashkim's name, Bashkim Beqaj's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a run-in in the past with Bashkim Beqaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me in detail what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He threatened me. It was a market day in Shtime that day. I was passing by a restaurant, a place where we eat bread. He came out and he told me to stop. He said that he had some business with me. Bashkim Beqaj said this. So I stopped. He invited me in, and I told him I didn't have time, but he then proceeded by saying that, "You were the one who brought my uncle to The Hague." And a person called Murat Musliu, he came and actually took him away because he wanted to beat him. This was the run-in. He was a young person. He could have beaten me. I'm an old guy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask a few detailed questions. Do you know which year this event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Last summer. I don't know the date because I have not been schooled. I have not completed any grade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he mentioned that his uncle was in The Hague, do you know who he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Well, uncle on his mother's side, Isak Musliu. He is his uncle on his mother's side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old would you estimate Bashkim Beqaj was last summer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Well, by God, I don't know his age. He is young. He's a youngster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after this event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: After this event, I went to Beqa -- to Murat Beqaj, Beqa's brother. And I said to him, your son nearly beat me in Shtime in reference to this matter. They felt very bad about it. They invited me inside, offered me coffee and tea, and they felt really bad about what had happened. They wondered how come their son did that to me. He said to me that Isak Musliu had called him six times from The Hague and told him to come to me, and I didn't want to do that. Did you understand what I was saying?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And let me follow up with a second question. Were there any other people present at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: No. Only his brother and Beqa himself. Before I went to them, Murat was outside, and took me to their house. And before I got in, I saw Beqa coming from the road with his wife. He greeted me. We went inside. They offered me tea, coffee, and they received me really well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you tell Beqa and Murat in relation to your testifying in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I told them to speak to their son, because the way he threatened me, if he threatened someone else in the same manner, something can happen to him. Beqa then said to me, my son will never do this again to you, and he will, on the contrary greet you wherever he sees you. He felt really bad about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen the son Bashkim Beqaj since that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I saw him. We had agreed to meet at Beqaj's place to discuss why he wanted me to go in and discuss that issue. I have a car. I saw them on the way. I called on them. Beqa came to me, but he didn't [as interpreted]. I spoke with Beqa and I said to him, "I'm here to discuss what had happened with your son. What does he have against me?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did his son greet you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: No, he didn't. I met him on another occasion, again, in Shtime. I greeted him, I spoke to him, but he didn't speak back to me. I told Beqa about this again. I said to him, "I spoke with your son. I spoke to him. He didn't reply. And you told me that he would do that. So I just wanted to inform you that I did speak to him but he didn't reply. And I'm an old person, he's a young man." And it's a tradition that a younger person should greet an older person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information about the contacts or relationship between Bashkim and his uncle Isak Musliu?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I have nothing to say about this. He was his soldier. He was his nephew. There is nothing else that I can add to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has Bashkim approached any other members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He said something to my brother's son. He invited him to a cafe for a conversation, but my brother's son did not accept this invitation, because he knew what was going to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Bashkim Beqaj has gone to any other member of your family's households to talk about Isak Musliu and testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I heard about this, but this is between them, between B1 and Beqa. This is between them. And I can't say anything about that. They can be put in the same room and discuss this, because this is not a matter for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point, I would like to show you a slide of a conversation and ask you for your comment. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we go in to closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go in to closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you please tell me what the six calls that Isak Musliu made to Beqa Beqaj were regarding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I don't know what the calls were about but something must have worried him because that's the reason he called. If he was clear about things, he wouldn't have called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were at the house of Murat Beqaj, drinking coffee and tea with Murat and Beqa Beqaj, at that point in time did Beqa Beqaj indicate to you what Isak Musliu wanted from him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: thing that Rexhe thinks that I was a person responsible for the -- their brother missing. Tell him that. And this is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. Dominguez, pay attention because some names have been mentioned and we will have to redact this from the transcript. But please be careful. The witness should be told to use pseudonyms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, may I please remind you to use pseudonyms for the names in front of you, the names of people we've spoken about, B1 and B2. Thank you. You were in the middle of answering. Can you please -- I believe you were saying that Beqa was telling you that Isak Musliu wanted he and Murat to do something. Can you please continue from that point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Beqa said to me that this is what he said, and I intended to tell you this, and since you were in conflict with my son, that's why I'm telling you this. But he didn't have the intention to tell me to help them in any concrete way. Can I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Beqa said to me, "I feel more sorry about you than for Isak. I would never give you up for Isak." This is what he told me. He said to me, "We are friends. We always were in good terms. We ate together, we drank together. Although he is my in-law, I would never give you up for him." This is what Beqa told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the Defence counsel wish to cross-examine the witness? MR. VAN DER SPOEL: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I have four questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be a good idea to have a break now. Half an hour break. And we will resume at quarter past 5. Thank you. Mr. Akerson? You wish to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. I'm sorry to interrupt. I had initially during the 73 bis conference indicated in the interests of saving time that we wouldn't call witnesses, two witnesses on our witness list. But we are moving so fast I'm wondering if I can call one of those witnesses anyways, because I think we will have plenty of time. I was thinking we would not get through this witness today. And I think we are going to have plenty of time to do that and to call the other witness. And that would be Howard Tucker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this will depend on how efficient you are. If I've understood you correctly, you've been extremely efficient this afternoon, but let sleeping dogs lie and if we need to, you can ask the Trial Chamber to grant you an amended schedule to call your witnesses. Thank you very much. Witness, you must remain seated until the usher drops the blinds again so that your identity remains protected. We shall resume at quarter past 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation] MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Thank, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Witness, you live in a small village, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Yes, you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I live in a small village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: You know a lot of people there, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Well, I know quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: My client, Mr. Beqa Beqaj, also lives in a small village, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He lives in Shtime now. He lived in our village, in Petrove, earlier, but now he is in Shtime more, more than he is in Petrove.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Is that also a small village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: You mean Shtime?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: No. Shtime is rather big. There are many people there. It is quite a bit city. It's a town.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Do you know any people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: In Shtime?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I have friends in Shtime, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you talk a lot with your friends about the trials in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Which friends? I don't know if I have spoken to friends about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: The friends you just mentioned you had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: No. I didn't have many conversations with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: I want to go back to the incident you talked about when you met my client's son, Bashkim. What time of day was it when you met him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: By God, it must have been after 3:00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Was it dinner time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: After dinner time, a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Did you meet him in the restaurant or near the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: Yes. It was a kebab restaurant. I was outside. He was inside. He saw me passing by. He called on me. He addressed me and said, "Uncle" -- or I don't know how he addressed me -- "Can you stop a little bit?" He invited me in. I told them I didn't have time to go in. And then he said to me, "You brought us to The Hague. You brought my uncle Isak to The Hague."

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: He acted strangely, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He acted in a cruel way, not in a good manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Is it possible that he was drunk, had too much to drink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: And were people drinking in that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: They were eating, yes. There were men eating. When he came outside, when I saw through the door, there were not that many people inside the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Were there any people you knew in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: The person who I knew came from out from the kebab restaurant, and he grabbed Bashkim by the arm and said, "Don't do this." And then I went to Beqa and told him that Bashkim threatened me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Who was the person who said, "Don't do this"?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: MR. VAN DER SPOEL:

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: What name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: If we are in public session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Witness, could you use a pseudonym, please, if you want to talk about someone who is protected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please proceed. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: The question was the name of the person, and if it's a person who is under protective measures, then probably we should go into closed session. Of course, I do not know the answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now turning to the Prosecution. Are we talking about a protected witness here or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: I also don't know who the name that the interpreter is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, to make sure, I would like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: To be on the safe side. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: MR. VAN DER SPOEL:

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Witness, is this person still alive?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he died. MR. VAN DER SPOEL:

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: When did he die?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He died a long time ago. After the dispute with Bashkim, he died two or three months after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Witness, were there any other bystanders who saw that incident with Bashkim on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: There were people inside but I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: You don't know their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: No. MR. VAN DER SPOEL: Mr. President, no more questions anymore, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the Prosecution have any other questions that arise from Defence counsel's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: I just want to point out that the name that was brought up from the witness, if we could redact that as a potential identifying factor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I quite agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: And if I can pose a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you mentioned that Murat died two it three months later. Do you remember when Murat died? Can you give us a date when Murat died, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: He died, but as for the date, I really can't help you with that because I don't know how to write and I haven't finished any school at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: Do you know if it was in the summer or winter of last year or which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: It was summer, last summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN
utterances.text: You mentioned that the incident with Bashkim took place in the summer as well. So I'd like to confirm Murat did die after the event and it was two to three months late sore that would place Murat's death at the end of summer and the incident with Bashkim at the beginning of summer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe he died two months later. Maybe before that. I really don't know the exact time. It would have been nice if I were able to take notes, but as I said, I don't have any school finished and I'm not in a position to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMINGUEZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dominguez. There are no other questions. Witness, thank you for your testimony, and I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a request. May I present that to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Beqa Beqaj is a good person, and it's hard to find someone like him, but his in-law made him, tricked him into these things, because he as a person was never a bad person. We never argued or had any dispute in the past. I would really wish for him to be set free and for us to go back home together, if this is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness, for that information. And once more, I wish you a safe trip home. As a precaution, please remain seated and I would now like to ask the Prosecution whether it's possible to call the next witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness that we were intending on calling will not be here until Wednesday. He's coming from the undisclosed country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, we will have our next hearing next Wednesday, in the afternoon, at 2.15 in the afternoon. If I'm not mistaken, Mr. Registrar, the hearing will be in the same courtroom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: Cross-examined by Mr. van der Spoel:
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.37 p.m.,
